Because the support for Azure was always not the best in OpenCode I created a new provider for OpenCode and other products using ai-sdk approach.

https://github.com/ophiosdev/azure-foundry-provider

## Highlights

- URL-first routing from copied Azure endpoint URLs (no model-name endpoint heuristics)
- Supports both chat and responses operation paths
- Supports Azure v1 operation paths and `/openai/v1` base root with mode-driven routing
- Chat transport uses OpenAI-compatible semantics (system role remains `system`, `max_tokens` is used)
- Request policy control for tools (`auto`, `off`, `on`)
- Built-in retries and 429 handling with exponential backoff + jitter
- Event-driven waiter queue for `maxConcurrent` admission (wake-on-release, abort-aware waits)
- Optional static quota controls (`rpm`, `tpm`, `maxConcurrent`, `maxOutputTokensCap`)
- Adaptive throttling from Azure `x-ratelimit-*` headers
- Request sanitization for chat history compatibility (removes assistant `reasoning_content`/`reasoning` fields)
- Automatic chat->responses fallback for model/operation mismatch errors (when mode is not explicitly forced to chat)
- Optional observability callbacks (`onRetry`, `onAdaptiveCooldown`, `onSanitizedRetry`, `onFallback`)
- Timeout support via `AbortSignal`

As I reviewed the compaction logic, it basically limits the compaction window to model input limit minus reserved limit to be able to get a summary of the history. The problem with Openai oAuth provider is that it has an input window of 272k and a context window of 1m.

So to actually use 1m context window the options I can think of are:
1. disable the compaction entirely.
2. use gpt-5.4 from another provider (like from opencode zen with 900k input window)
3. refactor the compaction logic to use another strategy.
4. configure the current compaction logic to use compacting agent input limits instead of current agent limits and set a compact agent with a larger input limit. considering the input limit of current agent since the summary goes there.

In my opinion, first option wouldn't be beneficial at all. Third and fourth options are long term and need a deeper analysis. Best short term solution here is either going with second option or using the model as it is.

ran into this too. dug into the code and here's what's happening:

the pending question state lives entirely in-memory as Promise resolve/reject callbacks in `question/index.ts`. when the process restarts, that map is gone. worse, the processor cleanup loop (`processor.ts:378-394`) actively marks any running/pending tool parts as `error: "Tool execution aborted"`, so the question ToolPart gets overwritten before anyone can recover it.

the thing is, the ToolPart on disk *does* contain the full question input (questions, options, headers) in `state.input` while it's in `running` status. so all the info needed to re-show the question is already persisted, it just gets destroyed on cleanup and nobody tries to restore it.

## Upstream fix merged

The root cause fix has been merged upstream: [bash-lsp/bash-language-server#1376](https://github.com/bash-lsp/bash-language-server/pull/1376).

bash-language-server now supports a `shellcheckExternalSources` boolean config (default `true` for backward compat). Setting it to `false` — via VS Code setting, LSP init param, or `SHELLCHECK_EXTERNAL_SOURCES=false` env var — omits the `--external-sources` flag entirely, preventing the unbounded memory growth.

### Updated status

| # | Fix | Where | Status |
|---|-----|-------|--------|
| 1 | `OPENCODE_DISABLE_LSP=true` env var | opencode | PR #16271 (open) |
| 2 | Make `--external-sources` configurable | bash-language-server | **Merged** — [#1376](https://github.com/bash-lsp/bash-language-server/pull/1376) |
| 3 | Per-process memory/time limits on LSP children | opencode | Not yet submitted |
| 4 | Share LSP instances across sessions | opencode | Not yet submitted — relates to #13041 |

### What this means for opencode

Once opencode bumps its bash-language-server dependency to a version that includes this change, users can set `SHELLCHECK_EXTERNAL_SOURCES=false` to prevent the memory explosion without disabling LSP entirely. PR #16271 (`OPENCODE_DISABLE_LSP`) remains valuable for headless sessions that don't need LSP at all.

## Upstream root cause fix merged

[bash-lsp/bash-language-server#1376](https://github.com/bash-lsp/bash-language-server/pull/1376) has been merged. bash-language-server now supports `shellcheckExternalSources: false` (config) / `SHELLCHECK_EXTERNAL_SOURCES=false` (env var) to omit the `--external-sources` flag.

This PR is still useful — headless `opencode run` sessions don't benefit from LSP diagnostics regardless of which language servers are involved. But the specific shellcheck memory explosion can now also be addressed by bumping the bash-language-server dependency and exposing the new config.

Seeing this in production with CodeNomad (desktop client for OpenCode).

OpenCode `serve` closes the `/event` SSE endpoint after ~7 seconds:
```
service=server method=GET path=/event status=started
service=server method=GET path=/event status=completed duration=7171
```

After this, the SSE stream never reopens server-side. The desktop client loses all events and the UI goes blank across all workspace instances.
